Class NitriteEntityOperations<T>

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.data.runtime.operations.internal.EntityOperations<T, RuntimeException>
io.micronaut.data.runtime.operations.internal.SyncEntityOperations<T, RuntimeException>
io.micronaut.data.runtime.operations.internal.AbstractSyncEntityOperations<NitriteOperationContext, T, RuntimeException>
io.micronaut.data.nitrite.runtime.write.NitriteEntityOperations<T>
Type Parameters:
T - The entity type
@Internal public final class NitriteEntityOperations<T> extends io.micronaut.data.runtime.operations.internal.AbstractSyncEntityOperations<NitriteOperationContext, T, RuntimeException>
Internal entity operations for Nitrite with automatic event firing and version handling. Uses ObjectRepositoryWriter for entity-to-Document conversion.

Save (INSERT) Operation: follows Jakarta Data @Save, which defines the operation by what the store holds rather than by the state of the identity field: an identity the store already holds behaves as @Update, and one it does not behaves as @Insert. So:

  • If the entity has no ID, it is inserted as a new document
  • If the entity has an ID that exists, the existing document is updated
  • If the entity has an ID that does not exist, it is inserted as a new document
A non-null identity is therefore never on its own taken as proof of a stored document. It never uses Nitrite's insert-if-absent update option.

Jakarta Data also requires the instance an insert or update returns to carry every value written to the database, including generated identities and incremented versions. An immutable entity cannot be given those in place, so what is returned is the replacement instance built here, not the argument.

Update (UPDATE) Operation: Replaces an existing document by ID, and never inserts. Requires the entity to have an ID. A document that is absent, or whose version does not match, affects no rows and raises OptimisticLockException. Jakarta Data @Update states both cases as one, and conditions neither on the entity carrying a version, so neither does this.

Since:
5.2.0

  • Method Details

    • update

      public void update()
      Micronaut's common save interceptor selects the update operation for a non-null generated identity. Jakarta Data save is conditional, though: the entity is inserted when that identity is not present in the store. Re-enter the save resolver here so the provider can distinguish that case from an explicit update operation.

    • getAffectedCount

      public long getAffectedCount()
      The number of documents the executed operation actually affected. A vetoed operation, or an update or delete of an entity without an identity, affects nothing.
      Returns:
      the affected document count

    • persist

      public void persist()
      Resolve Jakarta Data save semantics before firing lifecycle events. A non-null identity is not by itself proof that a row exists: both assigned identities and generated identities can be supplied for a new entity.
